content: The Minister for Health and Children in Ireland is the senior official within the Department of Health and Children in the Irish Government. This individual is tasked with overseeing healthcare services and related provisions across the Republic of Ireland. Currently, the position is held by Mary Harney, TD. She is supported by three Ministers of State: Brendan Smith, TD, who focuses on children; Máire Hoctor, TD, who addresses issues concerning older people; and Jimmy Devins, TD, who handles disability issues and mental health. Historically, healthcare responsibilities were part of the portfolio of the Minister for Local Government and Public Health until January 22, 1947. On that date, the role of Minister for Health was established, granting full authority over all health policy in Ireland. Over time, the health portfolio was occasionally combined with the social welfare portfolio, in which case the officeholder was referred to as the Minister for Health and Social Welfare. In recent years, particularly since Michael Noonan's tenure from 1994 to 1997, the role of Minister for Health has gained a reputation as a challenging and politically fraught position, often described as a poisoned chalice. This is due to the numerous scandals that have plagued the department, many of which stemmed from medical negligence. Examples include the Hepatitis C scandal, the unauthorized retention of baby organs without parental consent, the controversies surrounding Dr. Michael Neary in Drogheda, and other high-profile medical incidents. These events have often led to the Minister being directly associated with the fallout. Additionally, the Minister must contend with logistical challenges unique to the healthcare sector, such as strikes, resource shortages, and long waiting times, which are common issues in clinics and hospitals nationwide. The Minister's responsibilities include the development and evaluation of policies for the health services. The Department of Health and Children is divided into several key policy areas: 1. Child Care: This includes child care legislation and the National Children's Office. 2. Continuing Care: This encompasses services for homeless adults, individuals with disabilities, the elderly, and palliative care. 3. Finance: This area covers health insurance, hospital planning, and public-private partnerships. 4. Personnel Management and Development: This includes nursing policy and overall personnel management and development. 5. Primary Care: This involves community health services, such as child health, dental services, AIDS, reproductive health, and general medical services. 6. Secondary Care: This includes blood policy and hospital services. 7. Strategic Policy and Corporate Services: This area focuses on corporate services, health promotion, and health strategy legislation. The role of Minister for Health has evolved over time. From 1924 to 1947, it was part of the Minister for Local Government and Public Health portfolio. From 1947 to 1997, it was a standalone position as the Minister for Health. Since 1997, it has been known as the Minister for Health and Children. Ministers who simultaneously held the Health and Social Welfare portfolios are marked with an asterisk in historical records. Notably, Brian Cowen once famously likened the Department of Health to Angola, referencing the numerous landmines or challenges that exist within the department.
